children: Google CEO Sundar Pichai has indicated that the development of AI recursive self-improvement (RSI) remains in an early stage, suggesting that current AI systems are not yet fully autonomous in their model-building capabilities. This statement comes amid ongoing efforts by Google's DeepMind division, which utilizes AI loops and agents to assist human researchers in developing AI models. Despite advancements, Google has not observed notable end-to-end acceleration in AI research and development across various benchmarks. Pichai's remarks suggest that the industry is still far from achieving fully autonomous AI systems capable of self-improvement without human intervention.
Sundar Pichai's statement suggests that the development of AI RSI is still in its early stages.
The current market pricing for Anthropic's AI model reflects decreased confidence in its chances of being the best by October 2026.
Google's ongoing efforts in AI model development involve semi-automated processes rather than fully autonomous systems.

Watch for any further announcements from Google or its competitors regarding advancements in AI RSI. Developments in Google's DeepMind programs, particularly around the Gemini 4 Argon model, could influence market perceptions. Additionally, any new performance benchmarks or releases from Anthropic, Meta, or other key players may shift confidence levels in the race for the best AI model by the end of October 2026.

title: Google’s Pichai says AI self-improvement still in early stages
